# DG Delegated Full Review

Use this skill only when the user invokes it directly or an explicitly requested workflow invokes it. Do not select it automatically.

Use `$dg-engineering-writing-style` when available. Look for it in the repository's `./.agents/skills` folder.

Run the review outside the primary agent's context. Do not modify files, fix findings, or delegate from the review subagent.

## Workflow reference

May be selected by `$*-run-scoped-engineering-workflow` at step 6 through its review dispatcher. Standalone use remains supported. This skill owns the single review subagent; never route back through the personal dispatcher. Preserve any caller-supplied acceptance boundary alongside the review target.

## Resolve the target

- Preserve a pull request, branch, commit, diff, or other review target supplied by the user.
- Otherwise, review all staged, unstaged, and untracked changes in the current working directory.
- If the working tree is clean, review the current branch against its merge base with the configured upstream or default base branch.

## Run the review

Create exactly one read-only subagent or task in the current working directory. Use the host-specific path that matches the available tools without asking the user which host is running:

- In Codex, spawn a subagent (not a new user-visible task) and direct it to run `/review` for the resolved target.
- In Claude Code, use an `Agent` subagent and direct it to run `/review`, the alias for `/code-review`. Use `/code-review` if the alias is unavailable.
- In another agent host, use its task or subagent mechanism and give the worker the natural-language review instructions below.

If the worker cannot invoke the slash command, have that same worker follow these instructions instead. Do not start a replacement worker or perform the review in the primary context.

```text
Perform a read-only, defect-first review of the requested code changes. Inspect the complete diff and enough surrounding code and tests to verify each issue. Report only concrete, actionable regressions introduced by the change. List findings by severity with precise file and line references. If there are no qualifying findings, return "No findings." Do not modify files or delegate the review.
```

Wait for the worker to finish. Return its findings to the primary conversation, preserving priorities and file references. If the worker fails, report the failure instead of completing the review inline.

## Close the review task

Capture the result before cleanup.

- In Codex, close the completed subagent when a non-destructive close or archive action is available. Otherwise report that the runtime does not support cleanup.
- Claude Code subagents are ephemeral and need no separate archive action.
- In another host, close or archive the completed task when a non-destructive lifecycle action is available.

Do not permanently delete a transcript or worktree as a substitute for closing or archiving it.

  **Medium: clicking a type's name in the inline filter moves focus out of the editor, and then the next key closes the summon menu**
  - Location: apps/obsidian/src/components/NodeTypeFilterMenu.tsx:28-41 (`NodeTypeFilterRow`'s `<label>` wraps the checkbox, colour dot and name), now rendered inside apps/obsidian/src/components/NodeSummonMenu.tsx:318-330.
  - The summon menu keeps focus in the editor by cancelling every mousedown on its container (NodeSummonMenu.tsx:134-136). That stops a click on the checkbox itself from taking focus. It does not stop a click on the label text: in Chromium (and so in Electron/Obsidian), clicking a label focuses the checkbox it belongs to. Cancelling mousedown also blocks text selection, so nothing prevents that focus move.
  - What the user sees: they click a type name, which is the biggest target in the row. Focus moves to the checkbox and `view.hasFocus` becomes false. Then:

    - Typed letters no longer go into the `@query`.
    - Space toggles the focused checkbox.
  - So the filter breaks the "keep typing after filtering" flow the menu is built around. Clicking the checkbox square directly, or using "Only", does not have this problem. Advanced search's dropdown is unaffected because its panel is meant to hold focus.
  - Possible fix: for the inline panel, cancel the label's default behaviour and toggle by hand, or take the checkbox out of the label there. Another option is to put focus back on the editor after each toggle.
  - I worked this out from Chromium's label behaviour and did not reproduce it in Obsidian. It's worth a quick CDP or manual check: click a type name, then press ArrowDown.

  - The empty selection `[]` still means "all types", both in `filterCandidatesByNodeTypeIds` and in the panel's display and save conversions.
  - Advanced search behaves the same after the props were moved into `NodeTypeFilterPanel`.
  - "Clear filter" calls `closest("[data-search-dropdown-panel]")`, which finds nothing inline. That's harmless, because the editor keeps focus.
  - When the panel opens or closes, the menu's size changes and the existing size watcher repositions it.
  
  Checks: `vitest run src/utils/__tests__/nodeSummonResults.test.ts` passes (6/6), and `tsc --noEmit` reports no errors in the changed files.

The shared filter panel didn't change, so advanced search isn't affected. I added a check that clicks a type name and then presses ArrowDown, and it passes along with the other 8.

**Scope check** (ENG-2478): every change maps to a Done When line, so nothing is beyond scope.

**Standards check:** I found nothing to fix in the code. The PR is about 185 lines across 4 files. Three things are still outstanding before review:

- The PR needs a Loom video.
- `pnpm ci:validate` fails locally in `@repo/ui#check-types`, a package this change doesn't touch, with the same JSX type errors as before. A fresh `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` didn't clear it. The `validate` job passes in CI for the ENG-893 PR this branch is stacked on ([DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1617](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1617)), so it looks like a local setup problem.
